title: aidd eval standards --online --json
description: The standards check: each registry entry's evidence URL fetched again, and whether the sentence quoted as evidence is still on the page. It reads the registry and never edits it.

schema_version.description: The version of this output's shape. A new key keeps it; a renamed, removed, or retyped key bumps it.

checked_on.description: The day the pages were fetched.

limits.description: The bounds the run kept: each request's timeout, the whole run's time cap, the most bytes read from one page, and the most requests in flight (one or two; requests to one host are always one at a time).

max_seconds.description: The whole run's time cap, in seconds (--max-seconds); an entry not fetched by then is unreachable.

max_bytes.description: The most bytes read from one page (--max-bytes).

concurrency.description: The most requests in flight (--concurrency, one or two).

counts.description: How many entries ended in each status.

ok.description: Entries whose quote is still on the page.

moved.description: Entries whose address no longer serves the page.

missing.description: Entries whose page loads without the quote.

unreachable.description: Entries with no answer to judge.

results.description: One row per entry with evidence, in registry order.

releases.description: The release-feed check: one row per library standard whose tool has a feed (PyPI, npm, crates.io, Maven Central, NuGet, the Go module proxy, GitHub releases, go.dev, nodejs.org, the .NET release index, Adoptium, or python.org), in id order.

id.description: The library standard's id, such as `python/ruff-lint-format`.

registry.description: The feed the release was read from.

url.description: The feed's address for the tool.

checked_version.description: The version the standard records as checked.

latest.description: The newest stable release the feed named, never a pre-release; for a `latest_lts` standard, the newest LTS release where the feed marks one. Null when none was read.

status.description: ok: no newer major. newer_major: a newer major release is out (before 1.0, a newer minor); read its notes and update the standard. unreachable: no answer to judge; it says nothing about the tool.

reason.description: Why, in words; empty for ok.

status.description: ok: the quote is on the page (after a redirect, `final_url` names the new address). moved: the address no longer serves the page (HTTP 404 or 410, or a redirect to a page without the quote); find the new address and update `evidence.url`. missing: the page loads but the quote is gone; the source may have a new edition, so re-read it. unreachable: no answer to judge (a network error, a timeout, HTTP 401, 403, 429, or 5xx, a type that is not text, a page larger than the byte limit, or the time cap); it says nothing about the standard.

id.description: The entry's id in the registry's `standards` table, or an extension's name.

where.description: The first role, pack, or extension that applies it.

http_status.description: The HTTP status of the last response; null when none came.

final_url.description: The address the page was read from after redirects, when it differs from `url`; else null.

reason.description: Why, in words; empty for ok without a redirect.
